question: In the bubbling fluidized bed, why did the measured NO emissions fall as the NH3 co-firing ratio rose from 0 to 20% at a PA/SA ratio of 1:0?
expect: premise false: NO rose, from 169 ppm (0%) to 308 ppm (10%) and 325 ppm (20%) (sec. 3.3)
rendered:
Document 10: "Carbon-Free Ammonia Co-firing in Fluidized Bed Combustion: Analysis of Advanced Chemical Modeling and Detailed Mechanism"

Answer: The measured NO emissions fell as the NH3 co-firing ratio rose from 0 to 20% at a PA/SA ratio of 1:0 because, as the proportion of PA decreased, the amount of excess oxygen required for combustion was reduced, leading to more NH3 being consumed by reduction reactions rather than by NO formation at the low temperature of 1100 K.
